Documentation → Plugin Studio: build your own → Test and publish

Test and publish — from your desk to production

How a plugin goes from an idea to production safely — previews, rehearsals and test runs, the draft/testing/published gates, packages, signing and trusted publishers, and moving a plugin from a test SATOM to a production one with its datasets.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.plugin_studio studio.script_library
📍 WhereReport Studio (Lifecycle, Export, Import plugin); Plugin Studio (Test, Publish, Export package, Import app package); Plugins → Report Studio → Trusted publishers

The safe path#

  1. 1Buildin Report Studio / Plugin Studio, or in SATOM Builder
  2. 2TryLive preview (views), Simulate and Test with Rehearsal (apps), Test (scripts)
  3. 3Gatedraft → testing → published (views); Publish freezes a version (apps, scripts)
  4. 4PackageExport: a .satomplugin file, signed if built by SATOM Builder
  5. 5Test serverImport into a test SATOM, check, run with real people
  6. 6ProductionImport into production: the same checks run again there

Trying things without risk#

What How What it does not do
View — Live preview Report Studio editor Saves nothing; renders the unsaved body for you, with your data
App — Simulate Diagram tab Walks the saved draft as a rehearsal, asks you each question
App — Test with Rehearsal Test tab Steps that write are described, not executed
App — Test without Rehearsal Test tab Really writes (data stores, and the SATOM steps that write to devices): use test data
Script — Save and run the draft Script editor, Test Runs the draft in the jail with your test inputs
Anything — Test run in SATOM Builder Away from SATOM Runs on test data, with no network; nothing reaches SATOM or a device

The gates#

Views and widgets

  1. Draft — only holders of studio.plugin_studio see it.
  2. Promote to Testing — still only them; check the preview.
  3. Promote to Published — SATOM renders the saved body again and refuses if it fails. Everyone in the ADOM sees it under Custom Views.

You cannot jump from draft to published, and you can always demote.

Apps and scripts

  • You edit a draft; Publish freezes it as a version. People run the published version while you keep editing.
  • An app's Publish tab lists what blocks publishing (Fix before publishing), for example a connection without its secret.
  • Disable hides an app everywhere and stops every run without deleting anything.

Moving a plugin to another SATOM#

Export#

  • A view: Export in Report Studio writes <slug>-<version>.satomplugin.
  • An app: Export app package in Plugin Studio → Apps (a script app: Download the code).
  • From SATOM Builder: Download package (signed with the Builder's publisher key).

What a package carries:

Kind Carries Never carries
View / widget body.jinja, style.css, script.js, datasets, inputs, the definition of the administrator datasets it reads Rows
App Its form, diagram, actions, design, data stores (columns and rows), HTTP connections, API Catalog versions, images, the published scripts it runs Secrets: each connection's secret is typed on the server that imports it

Import#

  1. Import plugin (Report Studio) or Import app package (Plugin Studio).
  2. SATOM checks the package and shows what it would do: problems (refuse), warnings, what it creates and keeps, where it lands, who signed it. Nothing is written yet.
  3. Type the secret of each connection it creates, then Install.

Where it lands: an unsigned view in draft, a signed one in testing. Nothing lands published.

Datasets on the other server#

A view reads datasets by key. On import:

The dataset is On the destination
Built-in Always there
Device object (fortiweb_vip…) There once a device of that product is synced; otherwise dropped, with a warning
Administrator (admin_…) present there Used as it is
Administrator, absent there, carried in the package Created pending approval: an administrator reviews and publishes it in Administrator → Database → Plugin datasets; until then the view gets no rows from it
Administrator, absent, not carried Dropped, with a warning

Signing and trusted publishers#

A package built by SATOM Builder is signed with that Builder's publisher key. Register the key once on each SATOM (Report Studio → Trusted publishers, or from the Builder): its packages then read as signed and land in testing. A code plugin is never accepted unless Vision EBC signed it. → Manage trusted publishers.

A test SATOM and a production SATOM#

The recommended set-up:

  1. Build in SATOM Builder against the test SATOM (its datasets and objects mirror production).
  2. Validate on SATOM and Rehearse there, then Import.
  3. Let the people who will use it try it on the test SATOM.
  4. Import the same package into production — or import it through a production target in the Builder with a token allowed to import. Production checks it again with its own rules; administrator datasets it lacks arrive pending approval.

Checklist before publishing#

  • [ ] It renders / runs with no data (a new device, an empty store).
  • [ ] It renders / runs for a viewer with fewer rights (another ADOM, no maintenance devices, no audit permission).
  • [ ] Every optional value uses default(...).
  • [ ] Every write step has an error arrow to an undo or a message.
  • [ ] Datasets: only the ones it uses; administrator datasets published.
  • [ ] Connections: secrets set on this server.
  • [ ] Description and icon say what it is for.
